# Resource: stripe_file

A file uploaded to Stripe, such as dispute evidence, a business logo or an Issuing card logo. The provider uploads the local file that `source` names, and records the SHA-256 of its content. Stripe cannot change a file once it is uploaded, so changing `purpose`, or the content of the file, fails the plan.

~> Stripe cannot delete a file. `terraform destroy`, and a change that would replace the file, fail at plan time. To stop managing a file, remove it from the state as [Removing from State](#removing-from-state) shows; it stays in the Stripe account.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "stripe_file" "evidence" {
  source  = "${path.module}/receipt.png"
  purpose = "dispute_evidence"
}

output "file_url" {
  value = stripe_file.evidence.url
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `purpose` - (Required) The [purpose](https://docs.stripe.com/file-upload#uploading-a-file) of the uploaded file. Possible values: `account_requirement`, `additional_verification`, `business_icon`, `business_logo`, `customer_signature`, `dispute_evidence`, `identity_document`, `issuing_regulatory_reporting`, `pci_document`, `platform_terms_of_service`, `tax_document_user_upload`, `terminal_android_apk`, `terminal_reader_splashscreen`, `terminal_wifi_certificate`, `terminal_wifi_private_key`. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `source` - (Required) The path of the local file to upload. Terraform cannot send a file's content to Stripe, so the provider reads the file when it plans and when it applies. A file that does not exist yet when the plan runs, such as one another resource writes in the same apply, is read at apply time. When the file is gone from the path it was uploaded from, as on a machine that never had it, the plan keeps the recorded `source_sha256` and warns that it did not compare the content, so a changed file at that path goes unnoticed until it is there to read. Changing the path alone changes nothing in Stripe; changing the file's content is a change of `source_sha256`.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `expires_at` - The file expires and isn't available at this time in epoch seconds.
* `filename` - The suitable name for saving the file to a filesystem.
* `links` - A list of [file links](https://docs.stripe.com/api#file_links) that point at this file. See [`links`](#links) below.
* `size` - The size of the file object in bytes.
* `source_sha256` - The SHA-256 of the content of `source`, in hex, which the plan reads from the file, or the apply when the file does not exist yet at plan time. A file gone from an unchanged `source` keeps the recorded value. Stripe re-encodes some files, so its `size` is no measure of the content. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `title` - A suitable title for the document.
* `type` - The returned file type (for example, `csv`, `pdf`, `jpg`, or `png`).
* `url` - Use your live secret API key to download the file from this URL.

<a id="links"></a>
### `links`

The `links` attribute supports:

* `data` - Details about each object. See [`links.data`](#links.data) below.
* `has_more` - True if this list has another page of items after this one that can be fetched.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Always has the value `list`. Possible values: `list`.
* `url` - The URL where this list can be accessed.

<a id="links.data"></a>
### `links.data`

The `links.data` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `expired` - Returns if the link is already expired.
* `expires_at` - Time that the link expires.
* `file` - The file object this link points to.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `file_link`.
* `url` - The publicly accessible URL to download the file.

## Timeouts

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)

## Removing from State

To stop managing a file whose destroy is refused, remove it from the state without destroying it. In Terraform 1.7 and later, and OpenTofu 1.10 and later, replace the `resource` block with a [`removed` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/removed) and apply:

```terraform
removed {
  from = stripe_file.evidence

  lifecycle {
    destroy = false
  }
}
```

Using `terraform state rm`:

```console
% terraform state rm stripe_file.evidence
```

The file stays in the Stripe account. Replacing one with `terraform apply -replace` or `terraform taint` fails in the same way, at apply.

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import a file using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_file.evidence
  id = "file_1MqjB2LkdIwHu7ixcjxRlz9b"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_file.evidence
  identity = {
    id = "file_1MqjB2LkdIwHu7ixcjxRlz9b"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the file.

Using `terraform import`, import a file using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_file.evidence file_1MqjB2LkdIwHu7ixcjxRlz9b
```

~> Stripe does not return a file's content, so an imported file has no `source` or `source_sha256` in state. The first apply after the import records the configured `source` and the hash of its content without uploading it, so make sure `source` holds the content the file was uploaded with.
